relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled attribute arguments on the vulnerable path. For the staged parameter attribute, this statement produces a `ZEND_AST_ARG_LIST` with two children: a valid first argument (`self::class`) and the invalid dynamic class-constant second argument (`s->getAtelf::FOO`).

The flexible `attr->argv[]` storage is allocated from raw `pemalloc()` memory and vulnerable code does not initialize each slot to `IS_UNDEF` before later population and cleanup. Because the attribute is inserted into the attribute hash before all arguments are compiled, any fatal error during argument compilation leaves trailing `argv[]` slots uninitialized but still subject to destruction. The fix adds a loop that applies `ZVAL_UNDEF(&attr->argv[i])` for every declared argument.

ASan crash site. `zend_gc_delref()` dereferences the bogus `zend_refcounted_h *` extracted from the uninitialized `attr->argv[1]` slot during attribute cleanup, producing the reported wild-address READ.
At the selected `i == 1` cleanup iteration, `free_attribute()` reaches `zval_ptr_dtor(&attr->argv[i])` while the second slot still has non-`IS_UNDEF` type info.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `slot_type_info=3200171710` and `undef_type_literal=0` at `slot_cleanup`.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `attr_alloc.argv1_addr == slot_cleanup.slot_addr == 0x606000013248`; the fixed original preserves the same address equality for the clean second-slot cleanup.
The vulnerable original trace records `slot_cleanup.ref_argument == gc_delref_sink.gc_argument == 0xbebebebebebebebe`.
